subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw change isolated cron setup from a fixed 60s watchdog to the bounded job-timeout-derived policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96219, or require a different operator-tunable/configured policy first?
rationale: The source-confirmed fix is small, but it changes how long a truly stuck isolated setup can occupy cron capacity, which is an operational product tradeoff rather than a purely mechanical bug repair.

options.title: Accept the bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Merge or adopt the PR's 60s floor, half-job-timeout, 10-minute cap so slow healthy setup can complete while still bounding stuck setup.

options.title: Tighten the cap before merge
options.body: Ask for a lower cap or additional live proof if maintainers want stronger protection against stuck setup occupying cron capacity.

options.title: Require explicit configurability
options.body: Pause the bounded default and instead pursue a documented cron watchdog config surface with schema, docs, and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Merge or adopt the PR's 60s floor, half-job-timeout, 10-minute cap so slow healthy setup can complete while still bounding stuck setup.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent release and adjacent setup-timeout mitigation history make this the best available owner for the cron-capacity tradeoff decision.
